description: Cash held at central banks, treasury deposits maturing within 90 days, and highly liquid AAA-rated money market instruments. Includes Bank of Zambia correspondent balances and Citibank NY operational accounts.
AAA/AA-rated sovereign and supranational bonds held for liquidity management. Includes US Treasuries, German Bunds, and IMF SDR allocations. Marked to market quarterly.

accountName: Loans Receivable — Sovereign and State-Guaranteed (ADB Window)
description: Outstanding principal on ADB window loans to sovereign borrowers and loans carrying full sovereign guarantee. Interest rate based on LIBOR/SOFR + margin or fixed ADB rate (typically 2.50–3.25% p.a.).

Outstanding principal on African Development Fund (ADF) concessional loans to low-income African countries. Service charge 0.75% p.a., 40-year maturity, 10-year grace period. Funded by donor replenishments.
Outstanding principal on ADB private sector window loans without sovereign guarantee. Higher interest rate (5–7% p.a.) reflecting non-sovereign credit risk. Includes IDC Zambia industrial zone loan.
Specific and collective provisions for expected credit losses on the loan portfolio. Includes enhanced provisions for countries under debt distress, restructuring, or arrears. Reviewed semi-annually.

AfDB equity stakes in regional development banks, private equity funds (e.g. Africa Infrastructure Investment Fund), SME funds, and direct corporate equity investments under the private sector window.

Cumulative ADF grant disbursements for capacity building, budget support, and project preparation. Recognised as expense upon disbursement; this account tracks cumulative outflows for reporting purposes.

Interest income earned but not yet collected on sovereign and private sector loans. Also includes accrued commitment fees and service charges. Includes ZESCO/Republic of Zambia overdue semi-annual interest.

accountName: Property, Plant and Equipment — Net of Depreciation
description: AfDB headquarters building in Abidjan, 43 country office fit-outs, IT systems, vehicles, and office equipment. Depreciated on a straight-line basis over useful lives (3–50 years).
Prepaid expenses, staff advances, derivative fair value assets (hedging instruments on borrowings), and sundry receivables not classified elsewhere.

accountName: Bonds and Notes Payable — Market Borrowings
description: AfDB AAA-rated bonds issued in international capital markets to fund the ADB loan portfolio. Issued in USD, EUR, JPY, GBP, and local African currencies. Weighted average cost of funds approximately 1.8% p.a.

accountName: ADF Resources — Donor Subscriptions and Borrowings
description: Resources from AfDB member country ADF replenishments (currently ADF-16 cycle) and supplementary contributions. Deployed as concessional loans and grants to low-income African countries.
Interest accrued but not yet paid on outstanding bonds and bilateral borrowings. Includes currency swap settlements and hedging instrument payables.
Amounts due to suppliers, consultants, and service providers for procurement of goods and services. Includes project supervision bills, audit fees, and country office operating costs.
Fair value of interest rate and currency swap contracts in a net liability position. AfDB hedges currency mismatch between its multi-currency borrowing portfolio and USD-denominated loan assets.
Deferred income on front-end fees, pension liability (staff retirement plan), security deposits, and miscellaneous payables not classified under specific liability categories.

Capital paid in by 81 member countries (54 African, 27 non-African) representing the called portion of subscribed capital. Forms the foundation of AfDB's Aaa/AAA credit rating and leveraging capacity.

Contingent capital subscribed by members but not yet called. Provides the implicit guarantee underpinning AfDB's AAA rating. Can be called only in extreme liquidity scenarios. Memorandum account only — not on balance sheet.

Cumulative undistributed net income since inception (1964). Supports AfDB's capital adequacy ratio and provides a buffer against loan losses. General Reserve and Special Reserve components per AfDB financial regulations.

Cumulative donor contributions and transfers to the African Development Fund since 1972. Represents the concessional window's resource base, replenished every 3 years (currently ADF-16 at UA 8.9 billion).

accountName: Interest Income on Loans — ADB Window
description: Interest earned on ADB window sovereign and private sector loans at market-based rates (SOFR + margin or fixed ADB rate). Primary revenue source for AfDB institutional sustainability.
Service charges at 0.75% p.a. on ADF concessional loan outstandings. Nominal income; ADF operations are primarily donor-funded. Includes commitment fees on undisbursed ADF balances.
Front-end processing fees (0.25–1.00% of loan amount) and annual commitment charges (0.50% p.a.) on undisbursed loan balances. Incentivises timely project implementation by borrowers.
Returns on AfDB's liquidity portfolio (government bonds, supranational securities, money market funds). Managed conservatively in line with AfDB Investment Policy to preserve capital.
Donor contributions received under ADF replenishments earmarked for non-reimbursable grant operations in fragile states and post-conflict recovery situations. Recognised when conditions are met.

Staff salaries and benefits (2,700 employees), headquarters and country office operating costs, IT infrastructure, and institutional overhead. The AfDB administrative budget is approved annually by the Board of Governors.

accountName: Grant Disbursements — ADF Grants and TA
description: Non-reimbursable grant disbursements for budget support, capacity building, project preparation, and institutional development in eligible low-income and fragile African states.

Coupon payments on outstanding AfDB bonds and bilateral borrowings. Includes currency swap costs and hedging settlements. Positive net interest margin versus loan income is central to AfDB financial sustainability.

accountName: Project Supervision and Technical Assistance Expenses
description: Direct costs of project supervision missions, resident engineer contracts, independent technical audits, E&S monitoring consultants, and mid-term review expenditures across the active project portfolio.

Annual charge to income statement for new and increased loan loss provisions. Reflects expected credit losses on the portfolio including sovereign loans in arrears, watch list accounts, and non-accrual loans.
